correctness.rationale: For finite irreducible continuous-time Markov chains and farthest target distance d>=2, killing Q on a nonempty J subset of farthest targets yields analytic F_J(t)=A_J t^d+B_J t^(d+1)+O(t^(d+2)). Direct first-hit path integration gives A_J=W_d(J)/d! and B_J=[W_(d+1)(J)-L_d(J)]/(d+1)!, with L_d summing exit rates at PRE-hit vertices only. Exact inclusion-exclusion of no-walker-hit events and δ=N^(-1/d) give a two-term exponential expansion; the binomial-log F_J^2 term is O(N^-1)=o(δ) precisely when d>=2. A union bound controls nearer targets at order o(N^(-(m+1)/d)); finite irreducible hitting tails justify integration for any real m>0. Attaching a non-target pendant at a shortest-path vertex changes no d or d+1 first-hit paths, but adds r to one exit rate, changing B by -r W_v/(d+1)!, hence raises K1 strictly for unique farthest target. Independent killed-generator power expansions for the 4- and 5-state tree give (A,B)=(1/2,-2/3) and (1/2,-5/6), matching mean second coefficients 4/3 and 5/3.

originality.rationale: Kim-Lawley 2024/2026 arXiv:2310.07905v2 provides EXACT leading many-walker cover-time law K0 and shortest geodesic localization using inclusion-exclusion. The assessed result computes K1 from next-jump paths and prehit holding rates and establishes a concrete off-shortest-path perturbation. Lawley 2020 fastest passage gives first-order Weibull moments. Standard second-order extreme-value expansions might imply a SINGLE-J expansion but not the full target inclusion-exclusion/near-target truncation without extra argument.
residual_risks: An unsurveyed general second-order phase-type extreme-value theorem may give the single-target B coefficient by specialization.
The integration away from t≈0 uses finite irreducibility and fixed graph; invalid if target sets or rates vary with N.
The d=1 case is not included because binomial logarithmic correction enters at order N^-1.

value.rationale: The finite-state second-order coefficient separates geodesic products from exit-rate effects and quantifies exactly when/why the leading locality principle breaks. This is a motivated structural asymptotic with explicit counterexample on a tiny non-target pendant edge.

limitations: Fixed finite irreducible CTMC, iid walkers, all real m>0 and max directed shortest-hit distance d>=2; pendant locality-breaking statement requires unique farthest target and no initial mass at new leaf.
